newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gaddum - quick tender signals rates to remain steady.
newsitem.headline: Gaddum - quick tender signals rates to remain steady.

text.p: Bundesbank Vice President Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said on Friday the central bank's decision to inject extra funds into the money market signalled German interest would remain steady in the near-term, the Bundesbank said.
"With this decision we make it very clear that German monetary policy will remain unchanged in the near-term," a Bundesbank spokesman quoted Gaddum as saying.
Gaddum also said that this morning's quick tender was designed to stabilise money market rates at their recent levels around three percent.

The Bundesbank this morning injected 3.2 billion marks into the money market through a 5-day securities repurchase tender after call money rates had surged to 3.20 percent on Thursday from levels of around 3.05 percent on Wednesday.

The market had expected the add after the January minimum reserve target was set at an unexpectedly high 40 billion marks. Gaddum said the January target was higher than initially planned and that the central bank added funds in order to avoid a liquidity squeeze in the money market.
